subject: Segregated hosting: post-call confirmation & next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Ali Nasser <ali@kestrelhealth.com>
Cc: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 15 Apr 2028 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Segregated hosting: post-call confirmation & next steps

Hi Ali —

Thanks again for taking the time today. Quick write-up to capture what we heard and to confirm the immediate asks so we’re aligned internally. If anything below is off, flag it and I’ll update.

1) Goals and drivers
- Regulatory driver: Kestrel needs model inference to run in a fully segregated environment due to PHI and upcoming EU customer pilots.
- Primary objective: low-latency clinical inference with strict egress controls and auditability.

2) Key constraints you called out
- No outbound internet egress from model-serving instances; only approved outbound to your monitoring collector in the mgmt subnet.
- Customer-managed VPC with private subnets, internal-only routing between API gateway and model nodes; NAT gateway is disabled for inference nodes.
- Data residency: inference artifacts and logs must stay in your us-east-1 residency; archived logs can be exported to your secure S3 bucket under a lifecycle we agree on.
- FIPS-compliant KMS/HSM for key operations and envelope encryption for model weights.

3) Immediate asks we committed to today
- Redwood to produce a concise VPC connectivity checklist (I attached the draft PDF).
- Security questionnaire for SOC2 items + sample audit logs (we’ll provide a sanitized log extract).
- Sizing guidance: rough GPU count based on your 200 req/s P95 target — Jordan and Monica will follow up with a short sizing note.

4) Timeline & next steps
- Ben: send checklist + HubSpot update (today) — ACTION (done: attachments included).
- Jordan: sizing note and recommended model variant (EOD tomorrow).
- Monica: draft of the SOC2 evidence package and sample log (48 hours).
- Ali: confirm whether you can provide a network contact and a test VPC account (we can run a short connectivity smoke test).

Thanks — I’ll book a short follow-up for next week once Jordan has sizing.

Best,
Ben Carter
Enterprise Account Executive | Redwood Inference
ben.carter@redwood.com | +1 (415) 555-0147

Attachments: redwood-segregated-hosting-checklist.pdf (5 pages), kestrel-network-requirements.xlsx (stub)

From: Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Cc: Ali Nasser <ali@kestrelhealth.com>
Date: Mon, 16 Apr 2028 01:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Segregated hosting: post-call confirmation & next steps

Thanks Ben — adding a couple of technical clarifications from the infra side that we discussed. I captured them here so Ali and the network team can confirm.

- Egress policy: We can support the no-egress requirement by placing model pods on private subnets with route table entries only to internal load balancers. The monitoring collector will require a single allowed TCP/443 destination (IP or FQDN) — we’ll need that from Kestrel.
- DNS and certs: Because the instances won’t have public DNS, we recommend using an internal CA or invoking AWS Private CA; we can also support cert provisioning via SSM if needed.
- KV cache & HSM: For protection of KV cache (LLM state), we recommend encrypting at rest using your KMS with envelope keys. For HSM-backed signing operations we must coordinate key policies (Jordan, can you own the policy draft?).

Action items assigned: Jordan to provide GPU sizing + model variant recommendation; I’ll assemble a minimal network ACL/SG template for the VPC smoke test.

-Monica
Solutions Architect | Redwood Inference
monica.patel@redwood.com

Ben / Monica / Jordan —

Appreciate the clear summary. A few clarifications from our side:

1) Egress endpoint: we can allow a single outbound HTTPS endpoint to our Splunk collector (collector.kestrel.internal). We will provide the IP ranges during the integration phase.
2) Test VPC: we can provision a staging VPC in us-east-1 with one private subnet and a bastion host for the smoke test. Expect to share access next Tuesday.
3) KMS/HSM: our security team requires FIPS 140-2 validated HSM for key wrapping; we have an existing AWS CloudHSM cluster we can grant access to.
4) Logs: We need redaction rules applied to inference traces before any logs leave the environment. Can Redwood support in-line redaction (field-level) or will that be customer-side?

We’re interested in the trial but want the egress and HSM constraints explicitly documented in a short runbook we can sign off on. Please add the runbook to the HubSpot deal and share the draft.

—Ali
Director of Engineering | Kestrel Health
ali@kestrelhealth.com
